package.title: Lilly Says Online "Retatrutide" Isn't Its Trial Drug #shorts
package.description:
Lilly says retatrutide sold online as a "research peptide" isn't its trial drug. In that 48-week trial (adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition, no type 2 diabetes), the top dose averaged 24.2% weight loss vs 2.1% on placebo. It's still not FDA-approved as of September 2026.

This content is for educational purposes only and is not medical advice. Always talk to a qualified healthcare professional about your own situation. It's a prescription medicine. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

factcheck.summary:
This passes, with three optional wording fixes. All four sources exist and support the script.

- **Trial numbers (src1):** 24.2% vs 2.1% on placebo at 48 weeks in the 12 mg group matches. So does the population: 338 adults, BMI 30–50 or 27–29 with a weight-related condition, no type 2 diabetes. NEJM blocked direct access, so I confirmed these through ClinicalTrials.gov and a CME summary of the trial.
- **FDA warning (src3):** FDA's page (current as of 1 Sept 2026) warns about unapproved semaglutide, tirzepatide, retatrutide, survodutide and mazdutide "falsely labeled 'for research purposes' or 'not for human consumption.'"
- **Approval status (src4):** BioPharma Dive (23 July 2026) says retatrutide isn't approved. TRIUMPH-1, -2 and -3 have phase 3 results, and Lilly now plans to file in Q1 2027 after originally aiming for end of 2026.
- **Lilly's statements (src5):** Healio (14 Aug 2026) quotes Lilly calling the products "counterfeit," "entirely unverified, unapproved and not worth the risk," and falsely labeled research-use only "when they are intended for human use."

Safety is fine: no dosing, no sourcing, and the exact prescriber line is there. The title matches the content and the loop ending works.

The three fixes: "not its trial drug" is our paraphrase, since Lilly's actual word is "counterfeit." "Phase 3 results are in" overstates things a little, because several phase 3 trials are still running. And the s2 stat label should say it's the top dose.

issues.claim: Lilly says that's not its trial drug.
issues.problem: Lilly never says 'not its trial drug.' Its words are 'counterfeit' and 'not a medicine — it is entirely unverified.' The paraphrase is fair, but it's attributed to Lilly as if it were a statement. Using Lilly's own word is safer, and 'Lilly says' keeps it attributed.
issues.fix: s1 narration: "Seen retatrutide for sale online? Lilly calls those counterfeit." s1 on-screen: "LILLY: COUNTERFEIT". s6 narration: "Full trial breakdown on our channel. Because that vial online? Lilly calls it counterfeit." If the loop wording stays as it is, add 'Lilly calls them counterfeit' to s4 so the paraphrase is supported on screen.

issues.claim: Phase 3 results are in, but it's not filed yet.
issues.problem: Results are out for TRIUMPH-1, -2 and -3, but other phase 3 trials are still running. The unqualified line suggests the whole phase 3 program has reported.
issues.fix: "Early phase 3 results are in, and Lilly plans to file with the FDA in early 2027."

issues.problem: The pill doesn't say this was the top dose (12 mg). Shown on its own, it could read as the average across all doses.
issues.fix: stat_label: "Avg loss, top dose, 48 wks; placebo 2.1%"
